lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Hedged the bank's interest-rate risk on its fixed-rate bond holdings by buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
- Cut the monthly close from 8 working days to 5 by automating 30 reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Mapping 600 general-ledger accounts to a new chart of accounts, rebuilding the allocation rules and testing them against two prior closes, cut manual journal entries from 350 to 90 a month.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Trained 5 plant controllers on the new budgeting template and wrote its user guide.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Showed the share value fell from USD 50 to USD 40, a 25% drop, when the discount rate rose by 1 point.
- Raised the model's forecast accuracy by 12% across 10 years, from 70% to 82%, by adding rate-case timing.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Wrote onboarding notes on the fund's models for new analysts.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Replace the example LinkedIn URL with your actual profile, or omit it.
items.because: The profile should be current and consistent with the résumé.

items.says: Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It is not relevant to your qualifications and can invite bias.

items.says: Remove the nationality unless an application specifically asks for it.
items.because: If work authorization matters, address that directly instead.

items.says: Buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration would not generally hedge the stated interest-rate risk.
items.because: It would generally add similar interest-rate exposure.

items.says: Specify the exposure being hedged and the instrument or strategy used.
items.because: The hedging description needs to be technically accurate.

items.says: Clarify that the approval increase is seven percentage points, rather than a 7% relative increase.
items.because: The change from 41% to 48% could be described more precisely.

items.says: Give the number of applications reviewed and the period used to assess early defaults, if possible.
items.because: Those details help readers judge the strength of the finding.

items.says: Change “Writes” to past tense.
items.because: The role dates and other bullets describe completed work.

items.says: Clarify the period over which missed covenant tests fell from seven to one.
items.because: The measurement period is not obvious.

items.says: Substantiate how often the template was used or how many analysts benefited, if possible.
items.because: That would show its broader value.

items.says: Clarify how forecast error was measured and over what period.
Avoid implying that the forecast alone caused the debt paydown if other factors contributed.
Include a supported broader effect of the close improvements, if known.
items.because: Hours saved or fewer errors would show their effect beyond the timeline.

items.says: Add a concrete outcome of the capital-plan template, if available.
items.because: The stated result is process standardization rather than its impact.

items.says: Change “Mapping” to a past-tense action.
items.because: The bullet should be grammatically consistent and clearly describe completed work.

items.says: Shorten or clarify the sentence and its link between mapping and fewer manual entries.
items.because: The sentence is long, and that link should be easy to follow.

items.says: Discounting free cash flow to equity at WACC is a technical mismatch.
items.because: FCFE is generally discounted at the cost of equity, while WACC is generally used with FCFF.

items.says: Clarify your contribution and what the valuation informed.
items.because: The bullet describes a method but not its outcome.

items.says: Add a substantiated benefit of the training and user guide, or reconsider the bullet.
items.because: It may add less value than stronger quantified bullets without a resulting benefit.

items.says: Say when the market price was measured and what the comparison demonstrates.
items.because: “Within 6% of the market price” needs context.

items.says: Do not present closeness to market price as proof of forecast quality.
items.because: The valuation may have used information from the same date.

items.says: The drop from USD 50 to USD 40 is 20%, not 25%.
items.because: The decrease is measured from USD 50.

items.says: Clarify whether “1 point” means one percentage point.
Explain whether the forecast-accuracy metric was back-tested and how it was calculated, or remove it if it cannot be validated.
items.because: Accuracy across future forecast years cannot be established without actual results to compare against.

items.says: Keep the Regional Utility Valuation project only if it shows independent analysis or a distinct modeling skill.
items.because: It overlaps somewhat with the professional valuation work, which may have clearer business impact.

items.says: Specify what you personally did and what changed, or remove the bullet.
items.because: “Supported the FP&A team” is too broad to show either.

items.says: Specify what the performance report made easier to assess or which decisions it supported, if available.
Keep the onboarding-notes bullet only if there is room and it adds something distinct.
items.because: It is less compelling than the quantified experience.

items.says: Add other tools or systems in which you have real working proficiency.
items.because: Listing only Excel is likely too sparse for roles involving forecasting, reconciliations, and financial modeling.

items.says: Name relevant Excel capabilities if they matter to the target jobs.
Tailor and expand the methods list where experience supports it.
items.because: The list is brief compared with the work history.

items.says: Use consistent number, currency, and date formatting throughout.
Order bullets to lead with the work most relevant to each target role.
items.because: Credit roles and FP&A roles call for different experience to be prominent.
